title: IS12:: str2int.c (12.4)

lines.code: Source: K&R2, p43 (see also better version on p.61)
int atoi(char []); /* converts string to int */
lines.explanation: This is the prototype for function atoi defined below. It has one parameter that is an array of characters

lines.code: int getline(char [], int); /* reads string from input */
lines.explanation: This is the prototype for function getline defined below. It has two parameters: an array of characters and an integer
This array will serve as buffer for storing the user input (that is a sequence of characters).
During the evaluation of the condition part of this if statement the function getline will be called. It will read a line, place it int array buf and return the number of symbols read.

lines.code: printf("You have entered string %s and it was converted to %d\n", buf, atoi(buf));
lines.explanation: The function atoi will be called during the execusion of printf. It will take buf as a parameter, convert string buf into a number and return this number.
Function atoi receives an array of characters through its first parameter s
In each iteration of this loop we consider next character in the array s. The loop will stop when the character to be considered is not a digit
(s[i] - '0') will convert the digit stored at s[i] into its numeric representation (i.e., convert symbol '8' into number 8
When the loop is over, we return tha accumulated number as a conversion result
